newsitem.title: UK: Britain denies arms-for-oil deal with Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Britain denies arms-for-oil deal with Argentina.

text.p: The British government on Monday firmly denied a newspaper report suggesting it had agreed to relax an arms embargo against Argentina in return for a deal on oil exploration around its Falkland Islands colony.
"The embargo has not been relaxed," said a Foreign Office spokesman.

Anglo-Argentine relations improved in September 1995 when the two countries, which fought a war for control of the islands in 1982, announced agreement on a complicated deal on hydrocarbons exploration in waters around them.

The Observer newspaper said on Sunday that in return Britain had agreed to help re-equip the Argentine navy, allowing Rolls-Royce Plc to open negotiations to supply key components needed to repair engines in six warships.
It said the government was keeping the deal a secret because of concern it could inflame public opinion in the run-up to the next general election, which must be held by May next year.
But the spokesman said: "There is absolutely no link between the joint declaration with Argentina on oil exploration in the South Atlantic and the arms embargo."
Argentina claims sovereignty over the Falklands but its 1982 invasion was repulsed by a British military task force in a war in which about 1,000 people, mostly Argentines, died.
The two countries restored diplomatic relations in 1989.

In the 1995 agreement, Argentina agreed to allow the Falklands to bid on oil blocks closest to the islands, providing Argentine firms could also join the bidders. Licences are due to be awarded in a week's time.
The Falklands, in turn, agreed to allow joint United Kingdom-Argentina administration of other oil blocks that lie between the islands and Argentina.
